_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list
at run time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
source: 'schematic' means the net was traced on the Chapter 7
sheet cited in the note; 'inferred' means it was deduced from
the rails present at that slot and has not been read off a
schematic. appliedV: null means the rail was never traced --
shown as unknown rather than assumed safe.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides
what a shorted part does: A is an unfused 3 A rail with a
6600 uF reservoir, C is fused, E is a floating common.

C56.net: U16 MC1494L pin 14 (OUT) to the summing-amp virtual ground — anti-series with C57
C56.note: RESOLVED 2026-08 by the tantalum audit; was appliedV null, 'DC equals the multiplier output offset, which no manual publishes'. It is now traced on both ends and the answer is that neither plate carries a rail. Figure 7-15 sheet 1 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 60), zone B8 inside the dashed MULTIPLIER block: C56 and C57 are drawn in series in one vertical wire between two nodes. The lower node is U16 pin 14 (OUT), whose ONLY dc path is R32, 20 kOhm to S COM -- there is no pull-up to +15 S on this or on either of the other two multipliers. The upper node is the summing amplifier's virtual ground, the junction of R1 (2.0K MF feedback), R6 (2.0K MF), U3 pin 5 and the SUMMING AMP IN arrow; S5-18 step 3 names that node in those words. A virtual ground is 0 V and a pin with only a resistor to common is 0 V, so the dc across the pair is the MC1494's untrimmed output offset and no more -- millivolts. Recorded as 0 V rather than left null, the same call A5's C43 gets: the node was traced and the answer is that there is no working voltage across it. Read the polarity at 400 % and it corroborates this: BOTH '+' marks sit in the gap BETWEEN the two capacitors, so the joined positives are a floating midpoint and the outer plates are the minus ends. That is a non-polar pair, which is what a designer fits when the dc is about zero and its sign is not guaranteed. WORST CASE, and the reason a 10 V part here is not generous: with the PLL unlocked S5-18 step 11c puts TP7, the loop-filter output that drives these multipliers, at +13 V or -13 V, and a multiplier driven to its compliance or an op-amp that has lost its virtual ground could put 10-13 V on one plate. That is a fault condition, not service, but it is at or over the rating -- so if this board has had a PLL fault, replace all four.

C57.net: U16 MC1494L pin 14 (OUT) to the summing-amp virtual ground — anti-series with C56
C57.note: RESOLVED 2026-08. The lower half of the anti-series pair, its '+' joined to C56's at the floating midpoint and its '-' on U16 pin 14. Same sheet, same reasoning, same 0 V. See C56 for the trace and for the fault worst case.

C58.net: U19 MC1494L pin 14 (OUT) through R47 to the quadrature amp's virtual ground
C58.note: RESOLVED 2026-08; was appliedV null. Figure 7-15 sheet 2 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 61), zone B2, upper MULTIPLIER block: U19 pin 14 (OUT) sits on a node whose only dc path is R50, 10 kOhm to S COM, then R47 (4.7 kOhm) and C58 carry it to the QUAD AMP IN arrow. Sheet 1 lands that arrow directly on U6 pin 5, a 2006C inverting input with pin 6 to ACOM -- a virtual ground, 0 V. S2-134 confirms the routing: 'In the case of U19, the input signal is SUMMING AMP OUT, which changes the unity-gain frequency of the quadrature amplifier.' So both plates are at 0 V dc and the part is an ac coupling, not a decoupler. Unlike C56/C57 this one is a single polarised part with '+' toward the multiplier, which says the designer expected the MC1494's untrimmed offset to be slightly positive -- no offset-null pot is fitted on any of the three multipliers. Same fault worst case as C56: 10-13 V on the multiplier side if the PLL is unlocked or U6 loses its virtual ground.

C59.net: U15 MC1494L pin 14 (OUT) through R80 to the oscillator amp's virtual ground
C59.note: RESOLVED 2026-08; the twin of C58 on the third multiplier. Sheet 2 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 61), zone A2, lower MULTIPLIER block: U15 pin 14 with R79 (10 kOhm) to S COM, then R80 (4.7 kOhm) and C59 to the OSC AMP IN arrow, which sheet 1 lands on U9 pin 5 -- again a 2006C virtual ground. S2-134: 'In the case of U15, the input signal is QUADRATURE AMP OUT, which changes the unity-gain frequency of the oscillator amplifier.' 0 V across it in service; same fault worst case as C58.
